name: Helium recovery
principle: Helium is a trace component of some natural gases. It concentrates in the nitrogen-rich off-gas of the liquefaction or nitrogen-rejection unit, is upgraded to crude helium, purified, liquefied and shipped. Qatar's Helium 2 plant takes crude helium from six LNG trains.

process_steps.name: Helium-rich flash gas from LNG trains or NRU

suppliers.name: Linde Engineering
suppliers.product: PSA plus HISELECT helium purification hybrid with NRU

performance.basis: RasGas Helium 2, operational July 2013; with the existing plant 2 billion cubic feet per year

source.note: Gulf Times, New plant takes Qatar to top spot in helium export, 9 July 2013

performance.metric: share of global liquid helium demand met by the two Qatar plants

reference_plants.name: World helium supply by plant (Ras Laffan, Amur GPP, US BLM Cliffside)
reference_plants.capacity: Ras Laffan (Qatar): about 75-81 million m3/yr across three plants - roughly a third of world supply; Amur GPP (Russia): about 45-50 million m3/yr (designed up to 60 Mm3/yr); US BLM Cliffside (Amarillo, Texas) enrichment units; world production capacity about 360 million m3 (13 bcf) per year in 2023 (USGS)

source.note: USGS Minerals Yearbook 2023, helium chapter (world capacity 360 Mm3/yr); portfolio-pplus industry article 15 Mar 2026 (Ras Laffan 75-81, Amur 45-50 Mm3/yr); qatarenergylng.qa (three helium plants at Ras Laffan); read 2026-10-28

limitations: Needs large LNG or NRU throughput to be economic
Linde notes trace helium is vented where recovery is uneconomic
